data.narrative:
Blue Origin operates in Space & Aerospace at the SPAC stage, having raised $10B+ to date. The valuation universe comprises 5 public comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers including SpaceX, Rocket Lab, ICEYE, and Sierra Space, though no single peer set meets tight stage and tier alignment criteria.

Peer-Median triangulation is inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within the narrow peer set—only 1 same-stage data point exists against a minimum threshold of 3. Broadening to all 14 Space & Aerospace sector peers risks material distortion. Public-Comp Anchoring cannot be executed because the target's revenue is not disclosed; while the Space & Aerospace public median P/S stands at 27.4x across 6 tickers, application requires revenue figures unavailable for private companies.

The analysis finds no single triangulation method produces a defensible valuation range. Alternative approaches—such as DCF with disclosed capex and mission timelines, or precedent M&A multiples within commercial spaceflight—would require data not presently on file. The key uncertainty is the absence of Blue Origin's reported revenue or near-term financial guidance, which precludes standard comparable-company analysis. Any valuation narrative must acknowledge this structural limitation and, if a range is required, rest on scenario-based methodology rather than peer triangulation.
